subject: Biology
title: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
summary: The cell cycle is a cell growing, copying its DNA and dividing into two. Interphase (G₁ → S → G₂) takes over 95% of the cycle; the actual division (M phase) is short (about 1 hour in a human cell, out of a ~24-hour cycle).
In S phase DNA doubles (2C → 4C) but the chromosome number stays the same, because each chromosome now has two sister chromatids.
Mitosis (equational division): 2n → 2n, two identical cells — growth and repair. Meiosis (reductional division): 2n → n, four cells — gametes, with variation from crossing over.
Exam core: markers of each mitotic stage, the 5 sub-stages of prophase I (leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, diakinesis), and chromosome number and DNA content at each stage.

formulas.name: Phases of the cell cycle
formulas.formula: Interphase = G₁ (growth) → S (DNA synthesis) → G₂ (proteins for mitosis);  M phase = karyokinesis + cytokinesis;  G₀ = quiescent stage
formulas.mistake: G₀ cells are metabolically active; they just don't divide (unless needed).

formulas.name: Duration
formulas.formula: human cell in culture ~24 h (M phase ~1 h);  yeast ~90 min

formulas.name: Meiosis output
formulas.formula: 1 cell (2n) → 4 cells (n);  meiosis I reductional, meiosis II equational (like mitosis)

formulas.name: DNA content and chromosome number
formulas.formula: G₁: 2n, 2C → S/G₂: 2n, 4C → after meiosis I: n, 2C → after meiosis II: n, C
formulas.note: Chromosome number halves only in meiosis I (anaphase I); it doesn't change in S phase.

formulas.name: Cells and divisions
formulas.formula: cells after k rounds = 2ᵏ;   mitotic divisions needed for N cells = N − 1

formulas.name: Meiosis counts
formulas.formula: 1 meiosis → 4 pollen grains (or 4 microspores) → but only 1 egg (3 polar bodies/megaspores degenerate);  N pollen need N/4 meioses;  N eggs need N meioses

formulas.name: Prophase markers
formulas.formula: chromatin condenses into chromosomes;  centrosomes move to opposite poles;  by the end nucleolus, Golgi, ER and nuclear envelope disappear

formulas.name: Metaphase markers
formulas.formula: chromosomes on the equatorial (metaphase) plate;  spindle fibres attached to kinetochores;  best stage to study chromosome morphology

formulas.name: Anaphase markers
formulas.formula: centromeres split, sister chromatids (now daughter chromosomes) move to opposite poles;  centromere leads, arms trail

formulas.name: Telophase markers
formulas.formula: chromosomes decondense at the poles;  nuclear envelope, nucleolus, Golgi and ER re-form

formulas.name: Cytokinesis
formulas.formula: animal: a furrow in the cell membrane splits the cell in two;  plant: cell plate (middle lamella) grows from the centre outward;  karyokinesis without cytokinesis ⇒ syncytium (liquid endosperm of coconut)

formulas.name: Prophase I sub-stages
formulas.formula: Leptotene (chromosomes become visible) → Zygotene (synapsis, synaptonemal complex, bivalent/tetrad) → Pachytene (crossing over, recombination nodules, recombinase) → Diplotene (synaptonemal complex dissolves, chiasmata visible) → Diakinesis (terminalisation of chiasmata, nucleolus and nuclear envelope disappear)
formulas.note: Crossing over happens in pachytene; chiasmata become visible in diplotene — two different things.

formulas.name: Meiosis I vs II key events
formulas.formula: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate (sister chromatids stay together);  interkinesis: no DNA replication;  anaphase II: centromeres split, sister chromatids separate

examples.title: Counts at each stage
examples.problem: A cell has 2n = 16 and 2C DNA in G₁. Chromosomes and DNA in G₂, after meiosis I and after meiosis II?
examples.solution: G₂: 16 chromosomes, 4C. After meiosis I (each cell): 8 chromosomes (each with 2 chromatids), 2C. After meiosis II: 8 chromosomes, C.

examples.title: Divisions vs generations
examples.problem: How many mitotic generations and how many divisions make 128 cells from one?

examples.title: Meioses for pollen
examples.problem: How many meiotic divisions produce 400 pollen grains?

examples.title: Bivalents
examples.problem: How many bivalents (tetrads) are there in prophase I of a cell with 2n = 32?
examples.solution: A bivalent is a homologous pair ⇒ 32/2 = 16.

examples.title: Meioses for eggs
examples.problem: How many meiotic divisions are needed for 100 eggs (female)?
examples.solution: Each meiosis gives only 1 functional egg ⇒ 100.

examples.title: Significance of mitosis
examples.solution: Growth of multicellular organisms, cell repair (replacing gut lining, skin and RBCs), restoring the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio, and continuous growth in plants from apical and lateral cambium.

topics.title: Interphase
topics.explain: G₁: the cell is metabolically active and grows, without replicating DNA. S: DNA replication; in animal cells the centriole also duplicates (in the cytoplasm). G₂: proteins are made in preparation for mitosis. Cells that stop dividing enter G₀ (quiescent) — e.g. heart cells.

topics.title: Where mitosis occurs
topics.explain: In animals mitosis occurs only in diploid somatic cells; in plants it can occur in both haploid and diploid cells (the gametophyte also grows by mitosis).

topics.title: Significance of meiosis
topics.explain: It keeps the chromosome number of a species constant across generations in sexual reproduction (gametes n, fertilisation restores 2n). Crossing over and independent assortment produce genetic variation — essential for evolution.

topics.title: Synaptonemal complex and crossing over
topics.explain: In zygotene homologous chromosomes pair and are joined by the synaptonemal complex (synapsis). In pachytene non-sister chromatids exchange segments (crossing over) with the enzyme recombinase. In diplotene the X-shaped chiasmata are seen where crossing over happened.

topics.title: Long diplotene
topics.explain: In oocytes of some vertebrates diplotene can last for months or years.

topics.title: Meiosis II
topics.explain: After interkinesis, meiosis II begins without DNA replication — it resembles mitosis. In anaphase II the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate. The result is four haploid cells.

ratta: G₁ → S → G₂ → M;  G₀ quiescent.
S phase: DNA 2C → 4C, chromosome number unchanged.
Human cycle ~24 h, M phase ~1 h;  yeast ~90 min.
Prophase I: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene, Diakinesis.
Synapsis — zygotene;  crossing over — pachytene;  chiasmata — diplotene.
Anaphase I: homologues separate;  anaphase II: sister chromatids separate.
N cells need N − 1 divisions;  N pollen need N/4 meioses.
